deep.reconstruction:
The page contains no mathematics: no formulas, computations or derivations. It is a continuation of the German prose draft on the previous page. That draft belongs to Riemann's philosophical fragments 'Zur Psychologie und Metaphysik' (Naturphilosophie), written in dialogue with Fechner's 'Zend-Avesta'.

Content, in modern paraphrase:
(a) It completes the hypothesis begun on the previous page. Our nervous systems carry spatially and temporally bounded bodily processes, each spanning one primitive fibre and about 1/9 to 1/10 second. Their purpose is to bind external influences into a mental unity.
(b) When such a process ends, its bodily carrier is dissolved because its purpose is fulfilled. Its material constituents are excreted from the organism. Its mental expression (its content, the simple sensory idea) enters our soul.
(c) An interlinear insertion reads: 'The fact of memory leads to the hypothesis that ...'. Then comes item 3), numbered in the left margin and continuing items 1) and 2) on the previous page: with every act of thought something lasting enters our soul. This lasting something reveals itself as such only on particular occasions, but it exerts a lasting influence on phenomena.

This is a draft of the passage printed in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (Weber and Dedekind, 1876, 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts'). There the passage reads: 'Mit jedem einfachen Denkact tritt etwas Bleibendes, Substantielles in unsere Seele ein ...'. The printed version leads on to Riemann's notion of 'Geistesmasse'.

No mathematical problem is served. The only quantitative element in the context is the duration of an elementary sensation, about 1/9 to 1/10 s, which appears on the previous page. It is an empirical psychophysical estimate.
errors: No mathematical steps to check. The neurophysiological speculation (the carrier process is dissolved and its constituents excreted, one primitive fibre per elementary sensation) is obsolete 19th-century physiology rather than an error of reasoning.

results.what: Hypothesis that every elementary act of thought deposits something permanent ('Bleibendes') in the soul, which explains memory. In the printed version this leads to the concept of 'Geistesmasse'.
results.modern_name: Riemann's Geistesmasse / psychophysical memory-trace hypothesis (cf. later 'engram' concept)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's own published philosophical fragments (Werke 1876), influenced by Fechner and Herbart; the 'engram' term is due to Semon (1904)

results.what: Elementary mental unit as the expression of a spatially and temporally bounded nerve process; mental expression of a bodily process enters the soul when the process ends
results.usually_credited_to: Fechner (Zend-Avesta 1851, Elemente der Psychophysik 1860); Riemann's version is in his published fragments

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a philosophical prose draft with no mathematics. Its content corresponds closely to Riemann's already published fragment 'Zur Psychologie und Metaphysik' in the Gesammelte Werke, so nothing here is new or unattributed.
transcription_corrections: A marginal numeral '3)' stands at the start of the 'jedem Denkact' line, with a struck word next to it. This continues the numbering 1), 2) from the previous page; the line should read '3) [struck word] jedem Denkact tritt etwas Bleibendes in unsere Seele ein'.
The insertion 'Die Thatsache der Erinnerung führt zu der Hypothese, dass' is written interlinearly above the '3)' line, squeezed between lines.
Line 2: 'aufgelöst' is written above a struck word (illegible, perhaps 'zerstört'). The comma and 'sein Zweck ist erfüllt' follow.
Line 4: the word written above struck 'der einfache' is uncertain; it may read 'Inhalt' or 'Ausdruck'. After 'Vorstellung' a further struck word precedes the closing parenthesis.
Line 5: 'über' before 'ein' is struck, so the line reads 'tritt in unsere Seele ein'.
